cam-stock-setup.alt: Prism CAM Setup with a plate selected as the model body
cam-stock-setup.caption: Choose the model, name the setup and set stock allowances before generating operations.

cam-profile-preview.alt: CNC Profile preview showing passes around a plate and its operation panel
cam-profile-preview.caption: Profile preview for the plate, with 12 mm cutting depth and four holding tabs. Check the passes before confirming.

cam-toolpath-playback.alt: Toolpath Playback paused with a cutter visible on the CNC profile
cam-toolpath-playback.caption: Playback paused at 45 percent. The cutter marker shows its position along the programmed path; this is a motion preview.

cam-fdm-check.alt: FDM Preparation panel with the Azure bottle selected and nozzle settings visible
cam-fdm-check.caption: FDM preparation setup for the Azure bottle. Select the model and set nozzle, wall and overhang settings before running checks; this capture shows setup, not a completed report.

cam-resin-check.alt: Resin Preparation panel with a bottle selected and sampling settings visible
cam-resin-check.caption: Resin preparation setup for the Azure bottle. Sampling size and minimum feature size control the geometric screening; this capture shows setup, not a completed report.

assembly-components.alt: Two separate assembly components, a gray base and blue arm
assembly-components.caption: A gray reference base and blue moving arm, made into separate components before adding a joint.

assembly-revolute-setup.alt: Revolute Joint panel showing a face picked on each of two components
assembly-revolute-setup.caption: The two joint picks identify the reference component and moving component. The viewport shows their joint frames before confirmation.

assembly-drive-joint.alt: Drive Joints with the blue arm rotated to 55 degrees above a fixed base
assembly-drive-joint.caption: Drive Joints at 55 degrees. The joint handle and angle field let you check relative movement before setting up a motion study.

simulation-static-loads.alt: Static study setup for a cantilever beam with a support and applied load
simulation-static-loads.caption: The cantilever study has a fixed end and a 100 N downward load at the other end. Review supports and loads before solving.

simulation-static-stress.alt: Solved cantilever beam colored by von Mises stress with a legend and study settings
simulation-static-stress.caption: Solved example: a 100 N load on an aluminum cantilever, using a 5 mm element size. The legend is in MPa; these numbers describe this example only.

simulation-thermal-result.alt: Thermal result with a beam colored from 100 to 20 degrees Celsius
simulation-thermal-result.caption: Steady conduction with opposite ends held at 100 and 20 degrees Celsius. Read the temperature scale separately from a structural stress scale.

simulation-natural-frequency.alt: Natural Frequencies result displaying the first cantilever mode and its color legend
simulation-natural-frequency.caption: The first mode of the fixed-end beam is about 821 Hz in this example. Mode magnitude is relative; it is not a forced-response displacement.

simulation-motion-study.alt: Motion Study for an oscillating revolute joint with the arm in an intermediate pose
simulation-motion-study.caption: A two-second movement-only study of the revolute joint. The arm oscillates about its starting angle; masses and forces are disabled for this example.

simulation-pipe-flow.alt: Pipe Flow panel beside a tube with a 10 mm bore
simulation-pipe-flow.caption: Pipe Flow uses entered dimensions and fluid properties. This example uses a 10 mm bore, 100 mm length and 0.5 L/min; the tube illustrates those dimensions.

ecad-board-envelopes.alt: A green circuit board with mounting holes and three component envelopes in Prism
ecad-board-envelopes.caption: A rectangular board with mounting holes and approximate envelopes for a controller, connector and tall component. These are mechanical volumes, not electrical detail.

scan-mesh-quality.alt: Mouse housing mesh with aspect-ratio colors and highlighted narrow triangles
scan-mesh-quality.caption: Mesh Quality on a deliberately coarse tessellation of the mouse housing. The colors and highlighted triangles help identify areas needing review.

scan-section-sketch.alt: Section Sketch preview through a mouse housing mesh
scan-section-sketch.caption: Section Sketch fits editable curves through slices of the mesh. Here three parallel XZ sections are spaced 8 mm apart.

ar-export-panel.alt: AR Export settings for a camera lens, including scale and export controls
ar-export-panel.caption: AR export setup for the camera lens at tabletop scale. Export creates viewer files; sharing to a phone is a separate action.

freeform-cage-editor.alt: Edit Freeform showing the control cage over a smooth bottle
freeform-cage-editor.caption: The white control cage sits over the smooth Azure bottle. Edit the coarse cage to change the form rather than editing every rendered triangle.

render-image-settings.alt: Render Image panel beside a camera lens model
render-image-settings.caption: Choose image and lighting settings in Render Image before starting the render. The viewport shown here is the interactive model view.

materials-studio.alt: Appearance studio beside a selected duct model
materials-studio.caption: The Appearance studio edits the selected body finish. Engineering material assignment is available from the separate Materials tab.

assistant-modeling-panel.alt: Prism assistant panel open beside a camera lens model
assistant-modeling-panel.caption: The assistant panel sits beside the model so you can review its work. This capture shows the panel before a request is sent.

script-editor-workspace.alt: Python script editor and console beside a camera lens model
script-editor-workspace.caption: The Script workspace keeps the model, Python source and console together. This example reads the open model and fits the camera.

modeling-workspace-overview.alt: Prism Design workspace with a camera lens model, browser and document tabs
modeling-workspace-overview.caption: The Design workspace keeps document tabs, the model browser, ribbon and viewport together. Switch workspaces at the top for other tasks.

sketch-dimensions.alt: Sketch of a rectangular plate with two circles and dimensions of 80, 50 and 10 mm
sketch-dimensions.caption: An 80 by 50 mm profile with a 10 mm diameter dimension on the left circle. The remaining degrees of freedom are shown in the Sketch panel.

solid-extrude-preview.alt: Extrude preview of a plate profile with two holes and an 8 mm distance
solid-extrude-preview.caption: An 8 mm extrusion preview of the plate profile. The two inner circles become holes through the solid.

solid-extrude-result.alt: Completed extruded plate with two holes and an editable history
solid-extrude-result.caption: The confirmed plate retains its sketch and extrusion in the design history. Reopen the feature to change its depth.

drawing-workspace.alt: Editable A4 drawing sheet with four plate views, dimensions and hole center marks
drawing-workspace.caption: The plate as an editable A4 drawing: top, isometric, front and right views, with accepted overall dimensions, diameter annotations and center marks.

surface-zebra-inspection.alt: Zebra reflection stripes over a curved transition duct
surface-zebra-inspection.caption: Zebra stripes make changes in surface reflection easier to inspect. Look for how the stripes flow across the regions you are comparing.

solid-fillet-edges.alt: Fillet preview with the twelve edges of a box selected
solid-fillet-edges.caption: Fillet rounds the selected edges. This example previews a 2 mm radius on all twelve edges of a box.

solid-shell-result.alt: Completed open-top box with visible inner walls and a Shell history step
solid-shell-result.caption: A confirmed Shell removes the top face of this box and leaves 2 mm walls. The cavity and rim are visible in the finished solid.

solid-linear-pattern.alt: Linear Pattern preview of three rounded bodies with numbered instances
solid-linear-pattern.caption: Three instances of a rounded body, spaced 100 mm along X. The numbered preview helps check the direction and count before confirming.

nurbs-control-grid.alt: NURBS Control Grid panel defining a six by five point patch
nurbs-control-grid.caption: Control Grid starts a single NURBS patch. Here the panel defines a 90 by 60 mm patch, six by five control points and degree three.

nurbs-edit-control-points.alt: NURBS patch control net with one raised control point selected and its XYZ gizmo visible
nurbs-edit-control-points.caption: Edit Points shows the control net over the surface. One interior point has been raised; the selected point and XYZ gizmo show where the edit acts.

surface-loft-sections.alt: Surface Loft preview through three closed profiles listed in order
surface-loft-sections.caption: Loft passes through these three ordered profiles to form an open surface. The white section curves show the inputs; the blue sheet is the preview.

surface-thicken-preview.alt: Thicken preview adding a three millimeter wall to a lofted surface
surface-thicken-preview.caption: Thicken gives the lofted surface a 3 mm wall. The upper rim makes the added thickness visible; the panel controls the amount and direction.

freeform-soft-selection.alt: Freeform vertex selection and transform gizmo on a bottle control cage
freeform-soft-selection.caption: Vertex mode in Edit Freeform, with two vertices selected and a 60 mm soft-selection radius. The gizmo acts on the selection while nearby cage points can follow.

freeform-quality-review.alt: Freeform Quality marking poles and an n-gon on the Azure bottle
freeform-quality-review.caption: Check Quality marks cage topology on the smooth form: yellow poles have three edges, red poles have five or more, and blue marks identify n-gons. No comparison reference is selected here.
